Pumpkins harvest whole. Melons harvest as
Melon Slices
which must be crafted together to create whole melons. Melon harvests provide an average of five slices each while crafting a whole melon requires nine slices. This means that more melons must be planted than pumpkins.
Planting nine melons for every five pumpkins will give a balanced production rate. The farm should therefore be built in multiple groups of fourteen (nine melons plus five pumpkins.) This tutorial builds a 28-plant farm which is two groups of fourteen. Therefore, eighteen melon plants and ten pumpkin plants are needed.

Building the Farm
[
]
Farm Layout
See the image "Farm layout." The minimum area required is 21 x 12 blocks to contain the farm and machinery. The farm itself is 5 x 16. Dig a trench 14 blocks long. One bucket of water irrigates four blocks in each direction. So, place at least two buckets of water spaced to cover the 14-block length. Cover the trench with
Slabs
and place three torches spaced along the slabs.
Hoe out a 14-block strip on each side of the slabs and plant the melon and pumpkin seeds. At each end of the two plowed strips dig a hole and cover with a slab. This is to force the plants to place all of the melons and pumpkins in a straight line.
Rail Line
[
]
Rail Line Layout
See the image "Rail Line Layout" as a reference to directions used here. Place a
Solid Block
two blocks above the slab at the end of one of the planted strips. To the right of the block, dig a hole two blocks deep and place a
Redstone Torch
. Place a block of dirt over the redstone torch and then a
Powered Rail
on the dirt block. Add
Rails
parallel to the planted strips. When adjacent to the slab at the other end of the planted strip, place a powered rail and redstone torch. To the right of that, place a normal rail followed by an unpowered Powered Rail and a solid block.
Harvesting Contraption
[
]
Place a
Cart Assembler
over the right most powered rail pointing along the track and set the rotation control to Lock Rotation. Place a
Linear Chassis
on top of the cart assembler with the light-colored sides facing along the track. Place five more linear chassis forming a line to the left of the first linear chassis. Place a chassis under the second and last chassis from the right. Set the sticky range of all of the linear chassis to 1 by holding Ctrl while using a
Wrench
on one of the linear chassis.
On the side of the contraption facing the farm, attach a
Mechanical Drill
to the ground-level linear chassis using a
Slimeball
. Attach a
Chest
or
Barrel
above the mechanical drill closest to the rail. Using a slimeball, attach a
Portable Storage Interface
to the linear chassis above the cart assembler. Use the wrench to face the portable storage interface away from the chest or barrel.
Place a mine cart in the cart assembler then power it by placing a redstone torch or
Lever
next to the cart assembler. Pick up the contraption using the wrench, then remove the cart assembler and power source. Replace the powered rail that popped off when removing the cart assembler. Finally, replace the contraption while standing behind the rail line's end block. (This assures that the contraption will face the right direction.)
Setting a Timer
[
]
Place a
Redstone Repeater
facing into the block behind contraption's cart and set the repeater to four ticks delay.  Place a
Pulse Timer
with its output touching the input of the redstone repeater. Set the delay to 5 minutes or as desired. Place a lever touching the input of the pulse timer. Turn the lever OFF to enable the timer. The triangle on the pulse timer will be dim. Turn the lever ON (triangle is bright red) to inhibit the timer.
Crafting Whole Melons
[
]
See the image "Crafter from Above" as a reference to directions used here. The crafter accepts pumpkins and melon slices from the contraption through the portable storage interface which places all the produce on a short belt. The belt runs through two brass tunnels which feed the melon slices through the crafter and divert the pumpkins to a bypass belt. The whole melons from the crafter are placed back on the bypass belt and fed into storage along with the pumpkins. The device is powered by a horizontal windmill.
Crafter from Above
Building the Short Belt
[
]
Temporarily place a solid block on the ground next to the powered rail at the far end of the farm on the side away from the farm. Place two
Shafts
horizontal and end to end extending from the solid block away from the farm. Remove the solid block. Two spaces to the right of the far shaft, place another shaft in parallel. Place a
Mechanical Belt
between those two shafts.
Building the Crafter
[
]
Build a 3 x 3 vertical array of
Mechanical Crafters
beginning immediately to the right of the mechanical belt. On the back side of the crafter, use the wrench to join all of the crafters together. On the front side, use the wrench to set the flow pattern to converge on the middle crafter of the right column and eject the product to the right. Place an
Andesite Funnel
on the left side of the crafter array so that the mechanical belt will feed items into the crafter.  Place a chest or barrel on the right side of the crafter array against the middle block to catch the output of the crafter array.
Building the Bypass Belt
[
]
Place a solid block on the ground immediately to the right of the output chest. Place a shaft extending horizontally from the solid block pointing toward the farm. Remove the solid block. Place a mechanical belt between the two available shafts. Place a chest or barrel with an andesite funnel at the right end of the bypass belt. Place another andesite funnel on the crafter's output chest so that the items empty on the belt. Use the wrench on the top of the andesite funnel to make the triangle on the top point to the belt.
Installing the Item Handling Components
[
]
Place the two
Brass Tunnels
side by side on the two belts, one block to the right of the left end of the belts. Place a melon slice in the filter slot of the far side tunnel. Configure a
List Filter
to reject melon slices. Place the list filter in the filter slot of the nearside tunnel. Place a portable storage interface on the left side of the nearer tunnel then use the wrench to make it face toward the farm. On the back side of the portable storage interface, place an andesite funnel emptying on the end of the short belt. Use the wrench on the funnel to make the triangle on the top point toward the belt.
Power Source
[
]
Backside of the Melon Crafter Showing the Windmill
See the image "Backside of the Melon Crafter Showing the Windmill" as a reference to directions used here. Place a
Vertical Gearbox
on the ground with one of the shafts attaching to the shaft of the short belt where it touches the crafter. Place two more vertical gearboxes on top of the first one using the same orientation. On the side of the top gearbox facing the belt, place a
Cogwheel
to power the crafter array.
Place a
Rotational Speed Controller
on the ground one block in front of the bottom gearbox. Turn the rotational speed controller so that the shaft
does not
connect to the gearbox. Place a
Large Cogwheel
in the rotational speed controller so that it connects with the middle gearbox.
Place a
Windmill Bearing
so that its shaft connects to the shaft of the rotational speed controller. Place a solid block on the sticky face of the windmill bearing. Attach 32
Windmill Sails
to the solid block. Right click the windmill bearing to attach the sails and start the windmill. The direction on the windmill bearing does not matter. On the rotational speed controller, set the speed to 113 RPM and the direction to clockwise.
Operating the Farm
[
]
The farm is now ready to operate. With the contraption placed on the unpowered powered rail, momentarily turn the lever on and back off. The contraption will launch and the timer will start. The farm will run continuously until the clock is interrupted by breaking any one of the redstone dust lines. The farm will produce an average of 24 melons and 24 pumpkins per hour. You will need to either empty the final chest regularly or feed it automatically into a larger storage system.

Usage
[
]
A Millstone can be powered by a
Shaft
from below or by a
Cogwheel
from the side.
There are two ways to insert items into a Millstone:
Dropping items on top of it: anything that can be processed will be picked up if the input buffer is empty.
Hopper
s,
Funnels
,
Chutes
, and other inserters can directly feed it items from any side.
Once a valid item has been placed into the mill through any of the means listed above, the Millstone will begin to turn, and particles will appear around the machine. Once finished, the Millstone will not drop or output the result by itself, but there are two ways to remove processed items:
Right-clicking the Millstone with an empty hand: this will manually pick up everything in the output buffer.
Hopper
s,
Funnels
,
Chutes
, and other exporters can pull items out of the output buffer from any side.

[
]

Like the
Copper Backtank

from the
Shaft
at the top. The Air Pressure can also be used for tools like the

.

]
Netherite Diving Helmet
[

Together with a Netherite Backtank, this will protect you from extreme heat. To be effective, Legs and Feet have to be covered in

, too.
When Worn (Full set)
Provides immunity to
Fire
and
Lava
, slowly draining Air Pressure from the Backtank. Also grants improved vision in Lava.

[
]
A Wearable Tank for carrying Pressurized Air.
When Worn
Provides Pressurized Air to equipment that requires it.
When placed, Powered by Kinetics
Collects Pressurized Air at a rate dependent on Rotational Speed.

[
]
A pair of heavy boots, allowing for better traversal of the Ocean floor, including Oceans made of
Lava
.
When Worn
Wielder descends more quickly in liquids. Grants the ability to walk and jump underwater. Wielder also is no longer affected by

.

title: Overview
content:
Create is a Minecraft modification that reimagines automation through the use of
Rotational Force
, supplementing traditional redstone systems with a visually intuitive mechanical power network. Players generate and transmit kinetic energy to drive machines that move items, process materials, and construct dynamic contraptions. The mod also introduces
fluid handling
, enabling the transport and transformation of liquids using animated pumps, pipes, and spouts. A standout feature is its
realistic train system
, which allows players to build steam-powered locomotives, schedule routes, and transport goods or passengers across vast distances. To support learning and experimentation, Create integrates with the
Just Enough Items (JEI)
mod, providing in-game access to crafting recipes, machine usage, and sequenced assembly steps.
Item Processing & Automation
[
]
Create offers a multi-step, immersive approach to automation that goes beyond simple crafting:
Crushing Wheels
: Break down ores and blocks into finer materials.
Mechanical Press
: Compact items or shape metal sheets.
Mixers & Basins
: Combine ingredients into alloys, dough, or potions.
Deployers
: Simulate right-click actions for crafting or block interaction.
Sequenced Assembly
: Automate complex crafting recipes with precision timing.
Fluid Processing
: Fluids such as water, lava, and potions can be pumped, mixed, and dispensed using spouts, hoses, and smart pipes.
JEI integration allows players to view recipes and machine interactions directly in-game, making it easier to understand and replicate complex setups.
Moving Contraptions
[
]
Create enables dynamic, mobile machines that can rotate or travel through the world:
Mechanical Bearings
: Rotate entire structures like windmills or turntables.
Piston Contraptions
: Extend and retract block assemblies.
Minecart & Train Contraptions
: Build automated trains with customizable carriages, stations, and steam-powered engines. Trains can carry items, passengers, or entire contraptions across long distances.
Gantries
& Pulleys
: Move contraptions and structures vertically to create things like elevators and mineshaft drills,
Train systems are fully integrated with Create’s automation tools, allowing for scheduled deliveries, loading/unloading stations, and immersive transport networks.
Logistics & Transport
[
]
Efficient item and fluid transport is a hallmark of the mod:
Belt Networks
& Chain Conveyors
: Visually satisfying conveyors move items between machines.
Funnels
& Chutes
: Control item input/output with filters and timing.
Smart Pipes
& Pumps
: Transport fluids with mechanical precision, including vertical pumping and directional flow.
Redstone Link
: Wireless redstone communication for remote control.
Train Cargo
: Items and fluids can be loaded into train carriages and routed across stations using schedules and filters.
Return to
Tutorials

Usage

Packing
[
]
Main article:
Cardboard Package
When placed adjacent to any inventory, Packagers can create cardboard packages and fill them from the inventory they’re attached to. The process does not require extra materials.
Placing a written sign on the packager labels the created cardboard package with an address to be routed to.
There are two methods of commanding a packager to create a cardboard package: Redstone control and stock link control.
Redstone Control
[
]
When powered with a redstone signal, the packager attempts to fill the package as much as possible with whatever items are next in sequence in the storage block. A cardboard package has 9 slots of inventory. A redstone pulse will generate a single package. A continuous redstone signal will create a new package each time the output slot of the packager is emptied.
Stock Link Control
[
]
When a
Stock Link
is placed on a packager, the packager can receive requests from a
Logistics Network
. It can create packages with specific items, specific amounts of items, and a delivery address. The stock link must be attached directly to the packager and linked to a
Stock Ticker
or
Redstone Requester
which provide the stock link with the package request.
Unpacking
[
]
Placing an existing cardboard package into an empty packager will cause the package inventory to be moved to the attached storage block and destroy the package.

is a decorative block used to display items. It can be considered Create's counterpart to the vanilla Item Frame.

Usage
[
]
The Placard is primarily used to display items for decoration. It emits a short
Redstone
pulse, the same length as a stone button, when right clicked with the same item it is holding. Unlike
Item Frame
s, it will stick to
Contraptions
, and items cannot be rotated once placed inside. The Placard also does not interact with the Comparator; there will be no redstone output regardless of whether or not an item is inside the placard.

title: Pondering
content:
Pondering
is an in-game guide system that allows the player to quickly get information about Create blocks.
The pondering screen shows an example contraption that explains the functions of the block.
https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Windmill_Bearing_Ponder.mp4
The Ponder scene for a
Windmill Bearing
.
Contents
1
Usage
1.1
Keybinds
1.2
Navigation
1.3
Ponder Categories
2
History
Usage
[
]
The full Ponder Index can be accessed through the Create menu by clicking the
Engineer's Goggles
icon in the pause menu.
An item can be Pondered by hovering over it in the inventory and holding
forward
("W" by default) until the bar below the item is filled up. This displays an animated infographic about the item being pondered.
Keybinds
[
]
The keybinds for ponder are the same as those for certain player actions.
Q
- Activate Identify mode. This pauses the current ponder scene. Hovering over Create elements shows the name of the block and gives the option to ponder those elements.
S
- Restart the current animation.
A
or
D
- Go backwards or forwards a scene, if available.
E
- Close the animation.
Comfy Reading does not currently have a keybind, but can be enabled by tapping the button in the bottom right. This slows down the entire animation to help read the text boxes.
Navigation
[
]
While Pondering, similar or relevant machines can be viewed by clicking the icon to the left or activating identify mode and holding
W
over a visible component. After moving away from the initially pondered item, the option to "Think Back" can be found at the bottom left. The player can skip to specific parts of an animation by clicking different sections of the gray bar at the bottom.
The Ponder scene for a
Water Wheel
.
Ponder Categories
[
]
The categories ponders are sorted into in-game.
Kinetic Blocks - Components which help relaying
Rotational Force
elsewhere
Kinetic Sources - Components which
generate
Rotational Force
Kinetic Appliances - Components which make use of
Rotational Force
Fluid Manipulators
- Components which help relaying and making use of Fluids
Item Transportation
- Components which help moving items around
Logic Components
- Components which help with Redstone Engineering
Creative Mode
- Components not usually available in Survival Mode
Movement Anchors
- Components which allow the creation of moving
Contraptions
, animating an attached structure in a variety of ways.
Contraption Actors
- Components which expose special behavior when attached to a
Contraption
.
Block Attachment Utility
- Tools and Components used to assemble structures moved as an animated
Contraption
.
Railway Equipment
- Components used in the construction or management of
Train
contraptions
Recent Changes
- Components that have been added or changed significantly in recent versions of create
History
[
]
0.5.1
: Added a ponder category for recently added/changed blocks

Usage

Transferring Items
[

https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Portable_Storage_Interface_Ponder.mp4
The
Ponder
scene for the Portable Storage Interface.
Portable Storage Interfaces are used on
Contraptions
.
For Portable Storage Interfaces to interact they must face each other at 1 to 2 blocks apart. One interface must be on a
Contraption
, while the other is stationary.
The
Contraption
must have an inventory such as a
Chest
or
Barrel
, while the stationary interface has something inserting or extracting directly from it, such as a
Funnel
,
Chute
, or
Hopper
. Inventory will then be exchanged at the rate of the inserting or extracting component.
Contraptions
will stall when interfaces meet. A
Redstone
signal can be applied to break off the connection.
The connection automatically breaks off when no transfer has been done for a certain number of ticks. The default is 60 ticks, but the exact timeout is configurable via the
psiTimeout
setting. If the stationary side is not extracting items quickly enough (e.g. a funnel onto a slow belt), the connection may break off before the transfer is complete. To prevent this issue, extract the items from the stationary interface with a fast
Chute
directly into an inventory as a buffer, then use a
Funnel
to extract from that buffer onto the belt.

Mailbox names also support custom simplified RegEx syntax (check

Potato Cannon

100

The
Potato Cannon
is a projectile weapon that uses various food items as ammunition.

7
Usage
[
]
When fired while wearing a
Copper or Netherite Backtank
, no durability is used, rather, 4.5 seconds of air is consumed. If the Potato Cannon is fired while either not wearing a Backtank or wearing an empty Backtank, the cannon's durability is consumed instead.
When a Potato Cannon is held in both hands, the firing cooldown for both cannons is multiplied by
2
3
{\displaystyle \frac{2}{3}}
, resulting in a fire rate 50% faster than usual. The cannons alternate firing, rather than firing simultaneously. Ammunition with cooldowns below 15 ticks fire faster than the damage cooldown on entities, resulting in many shots phasing through the target.
A Potato Cannon can be enchanted with
Looting
,
Punch
,
Power
,
Unbreaking
,
Curse of Vanishing
,
Mending
,
Flame
, and
Potato Recovery
. Note until 6.0.11, power, punch, and flame do not function due to a bug.
[
1
]
Potato Recovery
gives all ammo a chance to drop as an item on hit. The chance of ammo being dropped is 25% for Potato Recovery 1, 33% for Potato Recovery 2, and 50% for Potato Recovery 3.
Power increases the damage a projectile will deal +20% damage per level.
Flame causes the target to take 1 damage every 10 ticks, for 40 ticks (2 seconds). This overrides the fire inflicted by the Baked Potato. Flame does not deal extra damage with Poisonous Potatoes, unless the attacked entity is immune to poison.
Blocks cannot be mined with a Potato Cannon held in the main hand.

title: Precision Workshop
content:
The precision workshop gives you the tools to build just about anything in the Create mod. In addition to the bulk mixing provided by the
Brass Workshop
, the precision workshop enables you to build
Precision Mechanisms
,
Crushing Wheels
, and
Train Tracks
. Precision mechanisms allow you to build
Rotation Speed Controllers
,
Train Controls
, and other advanced devices. Crushing wheels open up a world of automated ore processing for
Iron Farms
,
Nuggets of Experience
and more. This design does not include bulk washing or vanilla automation such as bulk smelting.
Precision Workshop
Precision Workshop
Contents
1
Production Centers
1.1
Bulk Mixer with Press
1.2
Precision Mechanism Line
1.3
Train Track Line
1.4
Mechanical Crafter Assembly
2
Power System
2.1
Stress and Speed Requirements
2.2
Method of Power Production
2.3
Converting Rotational Speed
2.4
Power Distribution
Production Centers
[
]
The precision workshop has four production centers which are described below.
Bulk Mixer with Press
[
]
Bulk Mixer with Press
This is a very compact combination of a high speed
Mechanical Press
and a
Mechanical Mixer
set up for heated bulk processing. The image "Bulk Mixer with Press" shows the layout. Rotational power enters from the shaft on the left connecting to the press which is two blocks above a
Depot
. The press passes rotational power on to a vertical gear box which turns a cogwheel driving the mixer. The mixer is placed two blocks above a
Basin
The basin is heated by a
Blaze Burner
below it, fed by a hopper on the left, and outputs to a
Mechanical Belt
on the right. The mechanical belt is powered from the mixer through the cogwheel on the right which feeds into a vertical gearbox that changes the axis of rotation to horizontal. A vertical belt conveys the rotation to the horizontal belt which conveys the mixer output through an
Andesite Funnel
into a barrel.
To operate the press, simply place an item or a stack of items on the depot. Pick up the items when the pressing is complete. For the bulk mixer, place the ingredients into the hopper on the left in the proper proportions. Feed the blaze burner a fuel item if needed. Collect the processed items from the barrel.
Precision Mechanism Line
[
]
Precision Mechanism Manufacturing Line
This is a basic manufacturing line for low-rate production of precision mechanisms. A fully automated production line can be found on the
Tutorials/Crafting Precision Mechanisms
page. The image "Precision Mechanism Manufacturing Line" depicts the design used in this workshop. Three
Deployers
are placed two blocks above a mechanical belt. Rotational power enters from the shaft on the left and is passed from one deployer to another. The first deployer has a cogwheel filter. The second has a large cogwheel filter. And the third has iron nugget. The process requires a lot of cogwheels and nuggets. The hoppers and barrels above the deployers allow you to stock a large number of components.
The manufacturing process begins by placing
Golden Sheets
in the barrel on the left. They are released one at a time to the conveyer belt. After the deployers add their components, the partially complete precision mechanisms are stored in the barrel on the right. You must then move the partially complete mechanisms to the left side barrel for the next round of components. The golden sheets and partially complete precision mechanisms must be run through the manufacturing line a total of five times before they are complete.
Train Track Line
[
]
Train Track Manufacturing Line
This manufacturing line is quite similar in design to the precision mechanism line described above except the right most deployer is replace with a mechanical press and both deployers are filtered with iron ingots. Unlike precision mechanisms, however, train tracks do not require multiple passes through the line. You can fill the input barrel with stone slabs and the deployer barrels with ingots then let the line run autonomously for true bulk production of tracks.
Mechanical Crafter Assembly
[
]
This workshop is designed to power the 21 mechanical crafters required to build a crushing wheel. You may, however, reconfigure the mechanical crafters for any other recipe with confidence that there will be sufficient power.
Power System
[
]
There are four factors which must be addressed when designing a power system: 1) stress and speed requirements, 2) method of power production, 3) converting rotational speed, and 4) power distribution. I will step through each of these.
Stress and Speed Requirements
[
]
This design has several devices with high stress-unit needs. The table titled "Stress Unit Requirements" lists all of the power consuming devices along with the stress units they consume at one RPM (SU/RPM). Multiplying the SU/RPM by the number of each type of device and summing the subtotals shows that the total consumption is 82 SU/RPM.
Stress Unit Requirements
Devices
SU/RPM
# Devices
Subtotal SU/RPM
Mechanical Press
8
2
16
Mechanical Mixer
4
1
4
Deployer
4
5
20
Mechanical Crafter
2
21
42
Total SU/RPM Required
82
The next step is to decide what speed (RPM) you want the system to run at. Each device could be powered at a different RPM, but for simplicity, this design is based on 64 RPM. Multiplying 64 RPM x 82 SU/RPM gives a total of
5248 SU
. We must now design a power supply that gives us at least that amount.
Method of Power Production
[
]
The first step is to decide upon
Water Wheels
, a
Windmill
, or a
Steam Engine
.
A water wheel produces 256 SU. A large water wheel produces 512 SU. Dividing the total power requirement of 5248 SU by 256 and 512 respectively gives a need for 21 water wheels or 11 large water wheels. That many water wheels would be an inelegant design.
A single windmill can provide up to 8192 SU depending on the number of sails used. So, a single windmill would be suitable for this workshop.
A single steam engine can provide up to 16,384 SU which is more than enough. But it is much more complex to build than a windmill.
A single windmill will, therefore, be the power producer for this workshop. The next step is to determine how many sails are need. A chart on the
Windmill
page shows the power produced for a given number of sails. You can calculate this directly, however, by noting that each group of eight sails adds 512 SU to the windmill's power output. Note that groups of less than eight add nothing. So, 8 to 15 sails produce 512 SUs, 16 to 23 produce 1024 and so on. If we divide our total requirement of 5248 SU by 512, we get that we need 10.25 groups of eight sails. Rounding that up to 11 gives us a need for
88 sails
.
Windmill Power System
Converting Rotational Speed
[
]
Windmills do not run at constant speed like water wheels do. Each group of eight sails adds one to the RPM. So, 11 groups (88 sails) outputs 11 RPM. We need to convert that to 64 RPM. A
Rotation Speed Controller
can do that very easily. But building a rotation speed controller requires a precision mechanism, which we won't have until we build this workshop. So, we will use
Adjustable Chain Gearshift
instead.
Each pair of fully-powered adjustable-chain gearshifts doubles the rotation speed. One set will double 11 RPM to 22. A second set will give 44 RPM. And a third would give 88 RPM which is more the 64 that we designed for. To get 64 instead of 88, we will power the third set of adjustable chain gearshifts with an
Analog Lever
rather than the standard lever used on the first two sets. An analog lever outputs an adjustable redstone signal strength which can vary the multiplication factor of the adjustable chain gearshift between 1.0 and 2.0. A signal strength of six on the adjustable chain gearshift gives a final rotation speed of 63.5 RPM...close enough.
Full Precision Workshop
Power Distribution
[
]
Getting the power from the generator to each of the components at the right height and axis of rotation is one of the most complex aspects of design. Running shafts and belts along with changing axes and directions of rotation can add a complex exoskeleton to your system. Many otherwise elegant designs become very messy when consideration of power distribution is left to the end.
It is best to think of power distribution in the early design of the system. Build your components first, the power distribution system second, and the power generator last. That will give you the most convenient location for the generator and avoid complex twists and turns in the power distribution.
Try to get the rotation inputs to all of your components aligned at the same height and direction. This makes the power distribution simple and efficient as can be seen with the single master drive belt at the back in the image "Full Precision Workshop."  Keep the power transmission devices (shafts, belts, gears, etc.) out of the way so they don't impede your movement. It is often easiest to run power for mechanisms overhead and power for conveyor belts underground. The image "Full Precision Workshop" shows that I kept the power distribution for the belts and mechanical crafters above ground. This was to make them easier for you to see. But I kept them at the back of the system so they would rarely be tripped over. The belt for the mixer is further forward than the others. Rather than putting a shaft across the front end of the workshop, which would get in the way, I chose to run a belt down from the mixer power. You can also add andesite or brass casings to the shafts either for aesthetics or ease of walking over them.

title: Quick Start Skill List
content:
Task
Purpose
Steps
1. Make Andesite Alloy
Andesite Alloy is a fundamental ingredient for nearly every item in Create. You will need
a lot
of it.
1. Mine iron ore and andesite blocks
2. Use JEI to find the recipe for Andesite Alloy
3. Make a full stack
2. Ride a spinning turntable
Rotational power is needed to run machines. Learn to generate power and control its speed and stress capacity.
1. Make a stack of
Shafts
. Use JEI for the recipe.
2. Make a half stack of
Cogwheels
.
3. Make a half dozen
Large Cogwheels
.
4. Make two
Gearboxes
. Consult the
Build Order
page and trace the dependencies for a gear box.
5. Make and install a
Water Wheel
.
6. Explore the use of shafts, cogwheels, and gearboxes to increase/decrease rotation speed and change the direction of rotation.
7. Build a
Turntable
. Place it on a rotating vertical shaft, then stand on it.
3. Make a Slimeball
Learn the use of a mill and some of the recipes it provides.
1. Build a
Millstone
and connect it to your rotational power source. Run it at the fastest speed you can.
2. Create
Dough
by milling wheat into flour and combining with a bucket of water on a crafting table.
3. Combine dough with
Lime Dye
on a crafting table.
4. Cut down a tree with a
Mechanical Saw
Build your first Create contraption! Build your starter workshop, learn about mechanical pistons, mechanical presses and gearshifts. See how the mechanical saw cuts down the whole tree at once.
1. Build a
Starter Workshop
2. Build eight
Piston Extension Poles
3. Build a
Mechanical Piston
4. Create 3
Iron Sheets
on a
Mechanical Press
5. Build a
Mechanical Saw
6. Build a
Gearshift
7. Place the mechanical piston on the ground horizontally with two extra extension poles.
8. Attach the gearshift to the mechanical piston and to a rotational power source.
9. Attach a
Lever
to the gearshift. This will allow you to move the piston in and out.
10. Coat the piston with slime from a slime ball, then attach the mechanical saw.
11. Activate the lever until the piston fully retracts.
12. Plant a tree two blocks in front of the saw.
13. When the tree matures, activate the lever to push the saw into the tree.
5. Mine some ore with a contraption
Create a minecart contraption. Learn about mechanical drills, cart assemblers, placement assist and the various issues influencing the design of mining contraptions.
1. Build a dozen
Mechanical Drills
2. Build 15
Linear Chassis
3. Build a
Cart Assembler
4. Build a
Wrench
5. Build a minecart, rail, and powered rail.
6. Build 2 chests.
7. Review
Tutorials/Mining Contraptions
and build a simple 3 x 4 mining contraption with manual rails and no portable storage interface. Use
Placement Assist
to keep the drills aligned.
8. Use the cart assembler to assemble the contraption and use the wrench to pick up the assembled contraption.
9. Lay rail along a tunnel in rock. Place the contraption on powered rail and give it a push to start.
6. Automatically Plant & Harvest Trees.
Learn to create brass, create electron tubes and smart chutes, build deployers, and automate log production
1. Create a half stack of
Electron Tubes
2. Build a
Brass Workshop
3. Create a stack of
Brass Ingots
4. Create 9
Deployers
5. Create one
Smart Chute
6. Follow the instructions in
Tutorials/Tree Automation
to build and run your tree farm.
7. Build an iron farm.
Learn how to build mechanical crafters, mechanical belts, encased fans and crushing wheels. Learn how to automate large scale ore processing.
1. Create a stack of
Brass Ingots
2. Build 21
Mechanical Crafters
3. Create 2
Crushing Wheels
4. Build 5
Encased Fans
5. Build a dozen
Mechanical Belts
6. Review the example in
Tutorials/Iron Ingot Automation
then design and build your own iron ore processor.
8. Build a Train.
Learn how to create precision mechanisms, sturdy sheets, and eight types of train components.
1. Build a
Precision Workshop
.
2. Build a
Precision Mechanism
3. Review the
Train
page and links for how to build a train.
4. Design and build your own train and rail system.
9. Build a Logistics Network.
Find your own way through the extremely powerful and complex High Logistics upgrade. Build mass storage systems, automated item retrievals, and fully automate resource management for factories.
1. Review the information and links in
Logistics Network
2. Design and build your own concept.
Feedback
[
]
Feedback really helps with projects like this. So please leave a comment below when you complete any of the tasks above and give some feedback on anything that can be improved.

title: Randomizer
content:
Introduction
[
]
Randomizer
is mechanism that dispenses different levels of signal randomly. Even though various variants of redstone randomizers existed, most of them had defects with compactness and regulation. Using Create modification, these defects can be fixed and modified as player wishes. So this page will help you construct your randomizer using simple components.
This is how working 3-output randomizer must look like. Golden blocks mean outputs of random signals.
Process of constructing is divided by steps for comfortable reading. Screenshots are provided.
Also should be noted that this is 3-output randomizer, which can be modernized up to 4-output one.
Construction
[
]
Step 1
Step 1:
Create a small platform 5x5 or 7x7 scale. Also you need 4 blocks high free space.
Step 2
Step 2:
Put three blocks, put dropper on top and hopper forward it.
Note: hopper must be set straight down.
Step 3
Step 3:
Connect
brass funnels
to dropper and vanilla hopper. Take attention to the arrows on them:
funnel
with dropper must be set as
taking in
,
funnel
with vanila hopper must be set as
extracting
.
Step 4
Step 4:
Connect vanilla hoppers to
chutes
that lead to dropper as shown in screenshot. The same must be done on the other side.
Step 5
Step 5:
Place
encased fan
facing into the
chute
and place underneath
creative motor
(if in Creative mode) or any other regulable source of
rotational force
for it to push items into the
funnel
. The same must be done on the other side.
Step 6
Step 6:
This step requires two different 64(16)-stackable items and one non-stackable item. Here we will use
wool
,
wooden axe
and
snowball
. Put snowball into the
brass funnel
filters
on the side and change droppable items number into 1, using mousewheel.
Take
filter
(
andesite
or
brass
one) and add wooden axe and wool into white-list. Put them on the other side of randomizer and also put droppable items number as 1.
Step 7: setting the filter
Step 7:
Since the main part is done, we have to make it into random signals. Put redstone comparators in front of vanilla hoppers; put block just forward the comparator
that will detect wool and wooden axe
. The snowball one can generate signal all by itself and we`re not going to touch it.
Step 7: filters are already put
Step 8
Step 8:
Make redstone contraption as shown on screenshot.
And... we`ve finished! The only thing you have to do now is to put wool, axe and snowball into the dropper and check the working. If something is wrong, please re-check your randomizer on mistakes.
P.S.
If you need unequal chances of signal outputs (for example, 50%-25%-25%), you have to add more items to create same ratio (for example, if you need 50%-25%-25%, you can put two wool, one axe and one snowball).
Enjoy your randomizer!
Modernization
[
]
4-output randomizer
Of course, this machine can be modernized up to 4-output randomizer.
Modernization of 4-output is actually a repeating of 7-8 steps, just on the second side, but we also take into filter
golden hoe (or any other non-stackable item)
along with snowball as non-stackable item and 16(64)-stacked item. The result must look like on the screenshot at the right. Most importantly, don`t forget to put golden hoe into the dropper for it to work properly.
P.S.
If you don`t like the output locations and you want to change it, you can use wireless
redstone link
to navigate the signal in 128 blocks range.

. These include the

Usage
[
]
Redstone Link
[
]
Redstone links transfer redstone signals across long distances, keeping their redstone signal strength. Receivers will output the strongest redstone strength received from sending links.
To toggle the redstone link between sending and receiving a signal, hold
Shift
and right click it or right click with a
Wrench
.  A redstone link in receiving mode will show a signal dish on the antenna.  Assign an item or block to at least one of the two frequency slots, and the redstone link will only send or receive signals to or from links with matching frequency slots.
The redstone link has a signal strength of a radius of 256 blocks, which does not require line-of-sight and thus can be placed underground, in a separate structure, etc.  Note that the redstone link seems to have a 'default state' of OFF, and any redstone links that are actively receiving when a world is saved will briefly pulse OFF when the world is loaded again; this can cause unintended behaviors in contraptions that rely upon heavily active links.
Redstone links can be remotely controlled using the
Linked Controller
added in Create 0.3.2.
Analog Lever
[
]
Emits a redstone signal with an adjustable strength. Right click to make it higher, shift right click to make it lower. The current signal strength can be viewed by looking at the lever while wearing
Engineer's Goggles
.
Pulse Extender
Pulse Extender
[
]
A pulse extender extends pulses. It emits a variable length pulse immediately after receiving a trigger signal. The output is normally off by default  and emits a powered pulse when triggered.
It can also be inverted to be normally on and emit a negative (power off) pulse by right-clicking it. Regardless of which mode it is in, the device will begin outputting a pulse immediately after detecting the ascending edge (off to on) of a redstone signal. The pulse will remain on as long as the trigger signal is on. The pulse length timer begins counting down only after the device detects a descending edge (on to off) of the trigger signal. Once the device is triggered, additional signal pulses will be ignored until the active pulse is complete.
Pulse Length
[
]
The pulse length can be changed by placing the crosshairs over the center of the device and moving the scroll wheel on the mouse. Pulse lengths can be set from 2-19 ticks, 1-59 seconds, and 1-30 minutes. The device will accept changes to the pulse length after the ascending edge trigger and before the descending edge trigger.  After the descending edge trigger, the device will accept changes that shorten the pulse length but ignore changes that lengthen it.
Circuit Behaviors
[
]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a pulse extender acts as a diode transmitting a signal only in one direction. It outputs a signal strength of 15 regardless of the input strength thus behaving as a circuit extender. And it can both power and draw power from opaque blocks.
Pulse Repeater
Pulse Repeater
[
]
A pulse repeater is a redstone device that emits a pulse a set delay after receiving a trigger signal. It can also be set to output a redstone signal by default and to emit a negative pulse after the time delay. Right-clicking the device toggles it between positive and negative pulse outputs. Regardless of the type of pulse selected, the device is triggered on the ascending edge of a redstone signal (off to on). Additional trigger signals will be ignored until after the pulse is complete.
Delay Settings
[
]
The delay can be changed by placing the crosshairs over the center of the device and moving the scroll wheel on the mouse. Delay times can be set from 2-19 ticks, 1-59 seconds, and 1-30 minutes. Once the device is triggered and the delay is counting down, changes to the delay time will not take effect until the currently triggered pulse is done.
Circuit Behaviors
[
]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a pulse repeater acts as a diode transmitting a signal only in one direction. It outputs a signal strength of 15 regardless of the input strength thus behaving as a circuit extender. And it can both power and draw power from opaque blocks.
Pulse Timer
Pulse Timer
[
]
A pulse timer acts like a clock circuit, repeatedly outputting a pulse with a manually-set time between pulses. The pulse timing can be between 2 tick and 60 minutes. Pulse timers can be inverted by right-clicking, causing it to be on by default with short off pulses.
Powered Latch
Powered Latch
[
]
A powered latch has two inputs (a set and reset) and one output. The side with the redstone torch is the output. The opposite side is the set line. Either of the other two sides can act as the reset line. A pulse to the set line will power the latch which will maintain a powered output until a pulse is detected on the reset line.  When the output is on, any pulses to the set line will be ignored. When the output is off, any pulses to the reset line will be ignored. Both the set and reset actions are triggered on the ascending edge of the pulse.
Continuous Signals
[
]
When continuous signals are applied rather than pulses, the behavior of the powered latch becomes more complicated. If the output is off when power is applied to the set line, the output will turn on regardless of the state of the reset signal. If the set line is subsequently turned off, then the output will remain on if the reset line is unpowered but will turn off if the reset line is powered.  If the output is on when power is applied to the reset line, the output will turn off regardless of the state of the set signal. If the reset line is subsequently turned off, then the output will remain off if the set line is unpowered but will turn on if the set line is powered.
Manual Operation
[
]
A powered latch can also be turned on and off manually whenever the signals to the set and reset line are the same. When they are opposite, the latch is locked in its current state and cannot be changed manually.
Circuit Behaviors
[
]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a powered latch can both power opaque blocks and can take signal inputs from opaque blocks.
Powered Toggle Latch
Powered Toggle Latch
[
]
A powered toggle latch has one input and one output. The output is on the side with the redstone torch. The input is on the opposite side. When a pulse is detected on the input, the power state of the output is toggled (off to on or on to off.) The latch reacts to the ascending edge of the pulse. The latch can also be switched on or off manually regardless of the state of the input signal. Similar to a redstone repeater, a powered toggle latch can both power opaque blocks and can take signal inputs from opaque blocks.
History
[
]

: Redstone Link recipe changed.
0.5
:
Pulse Extender and Repeater can now be inverted.
Redstone Link range changed to 256.
0.4
:
Added Pulse Extender.
Adjustable Pulse Repeater functionality given to Pulse Repeater.
0.2.4
: Redstone link receivers now emit their signal with the level of the strongest transmitter of the same frequency
0.2
: Added Analog Lever, Powered Latch, Powered Toggle Latch, and Adjustable Pulse Repeater.
0.1
: Added Pulse Repeaters and Redstone Links

The
Redstone Link
is used to send and receive redstone signals to other links.
Contents
1
Crafting
2
Usage
2.1

2.2
Sending and Receiving mode
2.3

3.1

4
History
Crafting
[
]
Name
Ingredients
Recipe
Redstone Link
Transmitter
+
Andesite Casing
2
Usage
[
]
Redstone links transfer redstone signals across long distances, keeping their redstone signal strength. When powered, a sending link causes receiving Redstone Links with matching frequency to emit redstone. The signal strength is kept. Receivers will output the strongest redstone strength received from sending links.
The redstone link has a 'default state' of OFF, and any redstone links that are actively receiving when a world is saved will briefly pulse OFF when the world is loaded again; this can cause unintended behaviors in contraptions that rely upon heavily active links.
Frequency
[
]
The frequency can be changed by right clicking the link's slots with an item or block. Assign an item or block to at least one of the two frequency slots, and the redstone link will only send or receive signals to or from links with matching frequency slots.
The link's frequency can also be copied and pasted by right-clicking with a
Clipboard
.
Sending and Receiving mode
[
]
To toggle the redstone link between sending and receiving a signal,
sneak
and right click it or right click with a
Wrench
. A receiving redstone link has a signal dish on the antenna.
Range
[
]
The Redstone Link has a range of 256 blocks, adjustable in the game
Config
. It does not require line-of-sight and thus can be placed underground, in a separate structure, etc.
Linked Controller
[
]
Main article:
Linked Controller
A
Linked Controller
can be used to activate receiving Redstone Links using player inputs.
Train Schedule
[
]
Main article:
Train Schedule
Redstone Links can be used as a schedule condition in
Train Schedules
. The Train network is loaded globally, so activating a loaded Redstone Link can satisfy a
Train
's schedule condition from anywhere. However, unloaded Redstone Links will not be considered in the schedule condition.

Right-click a

title: Rotational Force
content:
Rotational Force
is what powers the various machines and the contraptions in the Create mod.
Contents
1
Factors
1.1
Speed
1.2
Kinetic Stress
2
Transfer
Factors
[
]
Speed
[
]
Speed refers to how quickly a rotational component is spinning; it is measured in Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) and can be seen with a
Speedometer
. The maximum rotation speed of a component is 256 RPM by default (
Configurable
). Any component added to step up speed further, such as a cogwheel on a large cogwheel, will break off.
Speed can be controlled through several means:
https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Cogwheel_Ponder.mp4
The
Ponder
scene for the
Cogwheel
.
A
Cogwheel
and a
Large Cogwheel
can be connected together diagonally. One rotation of the large cogwheel is equivalent to 2 rotations of the small one, so the small one will always rotate twice as fast as the large one.
[
1
]
A
Rotation Speed Controller
with a large cogwheel can easily change the speed and direction of any input.
An
Adjustable Chain Gearshift
can change the speed of
Encased Chain Drives
connected to it based on redstone signal.
Higher speeds proportionally raise the stress requirement of a mechanical component. Twice the RPM produces twice the stress.
Kinetic Stress
[
]
Stress networks can be combined as long as they rotate in the same direction and speed where they meet.
Stress is the amount of energy mechanical components need to run and is shared across all components that are connected together in a network; it is measured in Stress Units (SU). The stress requirement or production of a certain component can be seen by looking at it wearing
Engineer's Goggles
and the total stress of a network can be measured with a
Stressometer
.
Each network has a total amount of stress units available to work with, which can be produced by
Generators
such as:
Hand Crank
Valve Handle
Water Wheel
Windmill Bearing
Steam Engine
Mechanical components utilize a certain amount of the SU available to the network depending on their type and the speed they're working at. If more Stress Units are used than are available to the network, it will become overstressed and stop entirely until more stress capacity is added or stress-generating components are removed.
Transfer
[
]
There are several ways to transfer rotational energy:
Shaft
- Transfers rotational force in a straight line. Some components have Shafts built in.
Cogwheel
- Inverts force, doubles or halves speed, can rotate axis 90 degrees. Some components have small cogwheels built in.
Mechanical Belt
- Relay rotation between 2 or more
Shafts
.
Encased Chain Drive
- Relays rotation, can rotate axis 90 degrees.
Adjustable Chain Gearshift
- When used with an
Analog Lever
, can manipulate speed between doubling or halving it.
Gearbox
- A miniature version of four connected
Large Cogwheels
.
Clutch
- Stops outgoing rotation when powered with
Redstone
.
Gearshift
- Inverts outgoing rotation when powered with
Redstone
.
Gantry Carriage
- Can move along a line of
Gantry Shafts
and outputs the rotational force when the shaft is powered with
Redstone
.
Sequenced Gearshift
- Allows for sequences of specific amounts of rotation.
Rotation Speed Controller
- Outputs a specified speed and direction of rotation.

Usage
[
]
Schematics can be used in the
Schematicannon
or
Deployers
. Before use, a Schematic's coordinates must be selected by right clicking and adjusting the position with the controls on screen. Shift right click to open an interface for entering exact Coordinates.
Making a Selection
[
]
Right click two blocks with the Schematic And Quill to select the area to be copied to the schematic. Right click again to name, save, and/or upload the schematic.
Saving the Schematic uploads it to the schematics file, allowing the Schematic And Quill to be used again. Save and Upload makes the Schematic And Quill usable in a
Schematicannon
or
Deployer
without the need of a
Schematic Table
.
Shift right click to remove the selection. Hold ctrl to highlight a block in midair and Scroll to adjust the distance. Once two blocks are selected, look at the selection's faces and ctrl-scroll to adjust the size.
Creating a Schematic
[
]
If a Schematic is saved to a file, it can be copied onto an Empty Schematic with a
Schematic Table
. This can be done across worlds.
Scanning and Printing Schematics in Create 1.14.3
In-game Tooltips
[
]
Empty Schematic
[
]
Used as a recipe ingredient and for writing at the
Schematic Table
.
Schematic
[
]
Holds a structure to be positioned and placed in the world. Position the Hologram as desired and use a
Schematicannon
to build it.
Schematic And Quill
[
]
Used for saving a structure in your world as an .nbt file.
Block States
[
]
The schematic includes Block State data for any block it includes and the
Schematicannon
and
Deployers
will restore the states as-is. This enables some Block State manipulation (e.g. saving and restoring
Composter
s at a near-complete state to gain more
Bone Meal
). More unusual manipulation can be achieved by using an NBT editor on the saved NBT file.

Usage
[
]
Cannon Prepping
[
]
A
Schematic
must first be positioned in the world before being placed in the cannon. Position the Schematic by right clicking. While holding the schematic, the selection and a control menu can be viewed.
The cannon will take the blocks required to build the structure from any adjacent inventories. The cannon will accept any inventory-type block as long as it has the function to output its contents.
The cannon feeds on
Gunpowder
, consuming once for every 400 blocks. The slot for gunpowder is located in the upper left segment of the menu, and may hold up to a stack at any given period. The cannon may consume up to 5 gunpowder when powered for the first time, and will have a bar for a fuel indicator next to the input slot. (Keep in mind that using Creative Crates will also allow infinite gunpowder)
Cannon GUI (Graphical User Interface) Breakdown
[
]
Input gunpowder
Input book for printed crafting ingredients list
Output of printed ingredients list book
Input Schematic
Start, pause, and stop cannon
Output blank schematic
Settings
Close dialog
Cannon Settings
[
]
In the bottom segment of the cannon's menu, there is a button that indicates the printer settings. Clicking the button will show a list of the following settings.
Solid Block Settings
[
]
Only one of the four following settings may be active at any given time. These settings indicate the behaviour of Schematic overlap with
Solid block
s in the selected area.
Don't Replace Solid Blocks - The cannon will never replace any Solid blocks in its working area, only non-Solid and Air.
Replace Solid with Solid - The cannon will only replace Solid blocks in its working area if the Schematic contains a solid block at the location.
Replace Solid with Any (Default Selection) - The cannon will replace Solid blocks in its working area if the Schematic contains any block at the location.
Replace Solid with Empty - The cannon will clear out all blocks in its working area, including those replaced by Air.
Miscellaneous Settings
[
]
These settings may be toggled independently of the other settings.
Skip missing Blocks - If the cannon cannot find a required block for placement, it will continue at the next location.
Protect Tile Entities (Default Selection) - The cannon will avoid replacing data holding blocks such as Chests.
Checklist
[
]
A
Book
or a
Clipboard
may be placed in the cannon's menu (currently located in the upper right segment of the GUI) to create a list of the required blocks in the form of a
Written Book
, factoring in the blocks available in adjacent inventories. The same book may be continuously re-used to update the checklist, given any changes to the adjacent inventory or the progress of the build.
Cannon Firing
[
]
Once the settings and all preliminary conditions are met for the cannon, the player may begin the firing process. Note: the cannon does not have to face the correct direction of the selected area, as it will self-correct during the process. In the middle segment of the menu for the cannon, there are 3 buttons that control the status of the cannon. Play, Pause, and Stop respectively. By default, the cannon begins in a paused state, with a yellow indicator on top. To begin the firing of the cannon, click on the Play button. This will activate the firing of the cannon, with a green indicator on top. If the player wishes to stop/end the firing, they do so by pressing the Stop button, which will function as if the Schematic is finished building.
The cannon will build in an additive method, beginning from the bottom layer and working its way to the top.
The cannon has a native limit for its range, which is 256 blocks from the schematic. It will only build given that the selected area is loaded within its respective chunk. Therefore, it's recommended that the cannon and player stay near the area of selection, or have another player be loading the chunks if used in a server. The cannon additionally may only build within its designated dimension.
Once the cannon finishes firing, it will play a 'Ding' sound to let the player know that the building process is complete. The menu will return to its stopped state, with a red indicator on top of the button. The Schematic consumed will then return into an Empty Schematic, which may be used again in the future.

Obtaining

Usage
[
]
Seats come in every color of
Dye
. They function much like a
Boat
in that they can be ridden by players and mobs. They retain this function while on a
Contraption
.
Lead
s can be
used
to seat mobs more easily. This also applies to seats on assembled
Contraptions
. Mobs can be removed from their seats by a
Deployer
or by right clicking the Seat (this will cause the player to sit in the mob's place.) They can also be removed by other
Contraptions
passing through the Seat. Players can leave the seat by
sneaking
.
Placed Seats can be dyed with
Dye
.
Trains
[
]
Main articles:
Train
and
Train Schedule
If a player sits in a Seat on a
Train
and enters third person mode by pressing
F5
, their view will be zoomed out further than normal. The amount can be adjusted in the
Config
.
If a non-
Blaze Burner
conductor is desired, a Seat must be placed directly behind the
Train Controls
.
A
Train Schedule
can be used to count the amount of players seated on a Train before leaving the
Train Station
. This can also be displayed with a
Display Link
.
Sitting in a Seat on a
Train
will also allow the player to stay on the Train as it passes through Nether Portals.

An assembly line creating

content:
Sequenced Gearshift
Renewable

No
The
Sequenced Gearshift
allows finer control over
Rotational power
, allowing multiple changes to the rotation over a period of time.
Contents
1
Obtaining
1.1
Crafting
2
Usage
3
Data values
3.1
ID
4
History
Obtaining
[
]
Crafting
[
]
Name
Ingredients
Recipe
Sequenced Gearshift
Electron Tube
+
Cogwheel
+
Brass Casing
Usage
[
]
The Sequenced Gearshift can be given up to 5 commands at a time. Each command can be adjusted by hovering over them and scrolling in the interface.
The first column consists of the commands
Turn by angle, Turn by Piston, Timed Delay, Await New Redstone Pulse, and End.
The first two are simply different measurements of rotation corresponding to
Mechanical Pistons
and
Mechanical Bearings
, the third makes the Gearshift wait before proceeding to the next command, while the fourth stops the sequence until the Gearshift receives another pulse. End signifies the end of a sequence, but is not necessary for a sequence to be completed.
The second column adjusts the measurements for each command. Up to 360 Degrees for Turn, 128 blocks for Piston, and 30 seconds for Wait.
The third column adjusts speed and direction. Here, rotation can be doubled, reversed, both, or neither.
A
Redstone Comparator
can be used to detect what instruction a Sequenced Gearshift is on. It will output a signal strength of up to 5, regardless of how many instructions are in the Gearshift.

The
shaft
is a basic mechanical component in Create. A shaft can be used to connect two mechanical components such that the rotation of one rotates the other, and shafts serve as the only blocks upon which
Mechanical Belts
can be placed.

Usage
[
]
Connecting components
[
]
When two mechanical components are connected to each other by a shaft, any
rotational force
provided to either component will be provided to the other component in addition to that component, at the same speed. As such, if both components provide
stress
, this can cause the machine to become overstressed.
Mechanical belts
[
]
A
Mechanical Belt
must be placed between two shafts. The shafts must be horizontal, parallel to each other, and perpendicular to the belt itself, and they must be aligned horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
Please note that you cannot have any other diagonal angles other than 45°.
Additionally, no obstruction can exist between the two endpoints with the exception of other shafts.
A
Brass Casing
can be placed over any segment of a mechanical belt, and this includes segments that contain shafts.

The Shelf is not obtainable by any means and only exists in the files of Create. Not much other information can be obtained about this block or the feature it was associated with as both were quietly removed in

Usage
[
]
Sliding Doors will automatically close when a
Contraption
starts to move. On
Trains
, the doors will only open when arriving at a
Train Station
, and close when the Train departs. Behavior can be adjusted in
Train Stations
. When used with
Elevator Pulleys
, behavior can be adjusted in
Elevator Contacts
. Sliding doors can also be prevented from opening by onboard
Contraption Controls
filtered for them.
When two Sliding Doors of the same type are placed together with opposing hinges, they will open and close together. Like other
Door
s, sliding doors can be interacted with while on
Contraptions
, and can be opened and closed with
Redstone
while not on an assembled
Contraption
.
Sliding Doors have a unique animation in which they slide into the adjacent block. Andesite and Copper Doors appear to fold into themselves.

Usage
[
]
If the Smart Observer is placed with the front facing a container such as a
Mechanical Belt
,
Funnel
or
Fluid Pipe
, it will emit a
Redstone
signal when an item is detected inside. A Smart Observer will also emit a signal if the block placed in front of it matches the filter.
If a
Filter
is applied to the Smart Observer, it will only emit a redstone signal when the item in the filter is detected.
Display Link
[
]
A
Display Link
can be used to display the inventory the Smart Observer observes. There are four settings:
Amount of Matching Items - Displays a number corresponding to matching items. It counts everything in the inventory if nothing is applied to the
Filter
.
List Matching Items - Displays the name of the items and the corresponding number of each item. It counts everything in the inventory if nothing is applied to the
Filter
.
Shortened - Shortens numbers above 999, e.g 1280 becomes 1k.
Full Number - Displays the full number.
List Matching Fluids - Lists the name of the fluids and corresponding number in milibuckets or buckets. It counts everything if nothing is applied to the
Filter
.
Shortened - Shortens mB above 999 to B (Buckets.)
Full Number - Lists all numbers in mB (milibuckets.)
Amount of Matching Fluids - Displays a number corresponding to matching fluids. It counts everything if nothing is applied to the
Filter
.
Portable Interface
[
]
Main articles:
Portable Storage Interface
and
Portable Fluid Interface
A Smart Observer used on a stationary Portable Interface can measure the inventory of the connected
Contraption
as a whole.

Using custom thresholds
[
]
Detecting whether the incoming power source runs above or below 30 RPM using a custom speedometer threshold.

title: Starter Workshop
content:
This starter workshop can be built with items sourced only from the
Overworld
. Even so, it packs a lot of power. With it you can build automated harvesting (though not replanting) of crop and tree farms and perform automated mining. You can also give your character important new capabilities and take advantage of a range of decorative elements.
Contents
1
Components
2
Layout
3
Power Source
4
Capabilities
Components
[
]
The starter workshop has the following components:
Crafting Table
Furnace
Stonecutter
Mechanical Press
with
Depot
Mechanical Mixer
with
Basin
Working Storage: 4x
Chest
Powering the mechanical press and mixer requires:
2x
Water Wheel
4x
Cogwheel
3x
Large Cogwheel
1x
Gearbox
2x
Shaft
Layout
[
]
Starter Workshop
The image "Starter Workshop" shows an efficient layout for the starter workshop. It is important to keep the mechanical press and mixer next to each other for easy linkage to the rotational power source. You can freely change the rest of the layout, add more furnaces, or add more storage.
Power Source
[
]
To design a power source, you first need to decide how many components you will have and what speed to operate them at. The wiki pages for
Mechanical Press
and
Mechanical Mixer
have charts that show the item production rates and required stress units for various RPMs.  For this design, I chose 32 RPM for the mechanical press which produces 2.6 items per second and requires 256 stress units. I chose 64 RPM for the mixer which produces 25 items per minute and again requires 256 stress units. This gives a total need of 512 stress units.
Power and Gearing
The next step is to design the RPM source. At this stage of game, you can build either water wheels or windmills. Windmills give better flexibility for power and output RPM, but for this low level of power requirement, water wheels provide a simpler design. Each water wheel provides 256 stress units, so you need two water wheels side by side to produce 512 stress units.
The final step is to produce the desired RPM for each of the components. The water wheel puts out a constant 8 RPM. Each pair of Large Cogwheel and Cogwheel, set diagonally, doubles the RPM. To get the 32 RPM for the mechanical press, you must double 8 twice. So, use two pairs of the cogwheel doublers to drive the press. The mixer needs 64 RPM so add one more doubler pair for that.
Note that the press must be driven by a shaft with a horizontal axis of rotation, but the mixer must be driven by a cogwheel with axis of rotation in the vertical. You can control the height of each output by placing the cogwheels on upper diagonals or lower diagonals of the large cogwheels. In this example, you need to gain height, so the cogwheels are always placed on the upper diagonal.
Capabilities
[
]
This starter workshop allows you to build all Create items up through level 6 of the
Build Order
chart. In a practical sense, this allows you to build a wide variety of
Contraptions
using components such as
Mechanical Drills
,
harvesters
,
saws
, and
pumps
; and motion anchors such as
Cart Assemblers
,
Mechanical Bearings
, and
Gantry Carriages
.
It allows you to improve your character's capabilities with
Diving Gear
and the ability to make
Enchanted Books
without leather (make pulp in a mechanical mixer, then press into
Cardboard
which can be used in place of leather.)
It also gives you new tools such as the
Wrench
,
Engineer's Goggles
, and
Toolbox
which help in building and debugging contraptions.
See the
Build Order
chart levels 1 - 6 for a list of Create components that can be made with the starter workshop.

Usage
[
]
Steam Engines use heated
Water
for power and are placed on
Fluid Tanks
, which are then used as a boiler. A
Shaft
can be used on the engine to create a kinetic output. The direction of said output can be adjusted through the
Value Settings
on the side of the engine.
Increasing the total power generated requires that one or more of the three characteristics (heat, size, water) of the
Fluid Tank
boiler be increased. This will increase the boiler's level to the lowest level reached by any of the three characteristics, increasing the maximum amount of SU Steam Engines are capable of generating from the boiler. A single Steam Engine can only extract up to 16,384 SU (The equivalent of 1 boiler level). To combat this, multiple Steam Engines can be attached to a single boiler to extract more power; however, this will not increase the total power generated by the boiler.
Boiler size
[
]
The tank size is the basic characteristic of a steam boiler. The required dimensions are affected by the heat supplied. For a passive steam engine (level 0) the boiler must be a 2x2 fluid tank of preferably one block height (making it any higher will be a waste of resources). For an active steam engine (level 1 or higher) the boiler must have 4 blocks per heat level. For example, a level 1 boiler must have a tank made of at least 4 fluid tank blocks, a level 9 boiler must be made of at least 36 blocks and a level 18 boiler (maximum achievable) must be at least made of 72 blocks.
Heat
[
]
A steam boiler requires heat to function. Heat sources must be placed underneath the boiler tank in order to affect it. All passive heat sources generate the same amount of heat. More heat can be generated with the help of
Blaze Burners
, which produce varying amounts of heat depending on their state.
and 25 lava dripstone generators are enough to sustain a level 9 steam engine

Water
[
]
Steam boilers also require water being pumped into them. The water requirements for a steam engine depend on its level, with higher levels consuming more water. If water is insufficient, the minimum required fluid transfer rate is shown in the Boiler status. To control the flow of water, you can use a
Fluid Pump
with a
Rotation Speed Controller
or another method for adjusting the pump's speed like an
Adjustable Chain Gearshift
. This allows you to achieve different fluid transfer rates for different engine levels.
When operating a steam engine, it's important to ensure that you have the correct amount of water flowing through it. For each level of a steam engine, you'll need to supply it with an additional 10mb/t of water. Note that rpm values of more 256 are impossible to reach without changing the upper limit through

Viewing Power Levels
[
]
Boiler status GUI when using
Enginner's goggles
Power levels can be inspected by viewing the boiler with the
Engineer's Goggles
or by attaching a
Display Link
to a
Display Board
. The required water input rate will also be highlighted in this display if insufficient. The levels are shown as a number representing the number of Steam Engines that can be attached.
The maximum number of power levels is 18. Eighteen Steam Engines each producing their maximum power of 16,384 SU gives a maximum boiler stress capacity of 294,912 SU. This can be achieved with the help of
Blaze Burners
fed
Blaze Cakes
(Super-heated Blaze Burners). For just a level 9 steam engine without
Blaze Cakes
, the maximum output is exactly half that amount at 147,456 SU.
Examples of configurations
[
]
Here are a few examples of valid steam boiler setups with no resource waste: (Sizes are in order of length, width, height)
Level 0 steam engine (smallest possible) - 2,048 SU
1x1x4 or 2x2x1 fluid tank
1 passive heat source under the tank (such as lava or a campfire)
one pump pumping water into the tank, running at 20 rpm
one steam engine attached to the tank
Level 1 steam engine - 16,384 SU
1x1x4 or 2x2x1 fluid tank
one heated blaze burner under the tank
one pump pumping water into the tank, running at 20 rpm
one steam engine attached to the tank
Level 4 steam engine (like in the picture above) - 65,536 SU
2x2x4 fluid tank
4 heated blaze burners under the tank
one pump pumping water into the tank, running at 80 rpm
4 steam engines attached to the tank
Level 9 steam engine (max achievable without superheating) - 147,456 SU
3x3x4 fluid tank
9 heated blaze burners under the tank
one pump pumping water into the tank, running at 180 rpm
9 steam engines attached to the tank
Level 18 steam engine (max achievable via superheating) - 294,912 SU
3x3x8 fluid tank
9 superheated blaze burners under the tank
two pumps pumping water into the tank, running at 180 rpm each
18 steam engines attached to the tank
Each steam engine extracts
up to
16,384 SU. If the boiler is at a lower level, the steam engines equally divide the total output. For example, if a fuel runs out on a level 9 steam engine, it becomes a level 0 steam engine with a total output of 2,048 SU. Each of the 9 steam engine shafts outputs 2048/9=227.56 SU.
Trivia
[
]
Steam Engines can overstress separately. This means that if one overstresses, the rest will continue to generate rotational force. This makes it possible to make a self-sufficient steam engine that never binds up.
Unlike machines in various other mods, which may use only a small amount of water and store excess for later, a Steam Engine setup does not store water, despite being made of Fluid Tanks. Water is "evaporated" upon insertion whether it surpasses the requirements of the engine or not, and any liquid stored beforehand in the Fluid Tank is instantly voided.
For active steam boilers, the blaze burners can be automatically fueled, via mechanical arms or deployers. In order to remain functional, an active steam engine requires a renewable supply of fuel which is usually achieved by either a lava or charcoal farm.
Eggs are a fuel source for blaze burners. Therfore you can make a self sufficient level 9 engine with only eggs. This method holds the record for smallest level 9 steam engine.
Troubleshooting
[
]
Occasionally your steam engine may show that it has no water intake despite having a water pump going into it. The only way to fix this is to remove all steam engines so that the tank reverts back to a normal fluid tank and then replacing them.
By holding right click on the side of a steam engine you can change which direction it rotates. If your factory seems to be running backwards then this is a quick way to fix it.
If your steam engine isn't moving despite the fact that you're feeding it water, make sure that the pump feeding it is running at at least 20 RPM.
There is a
known issue
where steam engines tend to spin down unevenly when power is removed. This can be partially overcome by avoiding having breakable connections between engines and using
Encased Chain Drive
or
Mechanical Belts
to merge power output instead.

Usage
[
]
The Steam Whistle can be placed on
Fluid Tanks
. The Tank must have a heat source beneath it for the Whistle to function. It can be activated by
Redstone
. Right click with a Whistle in hand to extend it. The Whistle can be extended up to 12 times, playing up to 13 notes per octave.
Use
a
Wrench
to change the octave; 3 octaves are available.
Engineer's Goggles
can be used to view the current note.
Steam Whistles will also function on
Trains
, complete with a different set of sounds. While driving the train, use the
sprint
key to blow the whistle. The Whistle's pitch will be accounted for. Non-player conductors will also blow the whistles shortly before arriving at distant stations.
Main article:
Trains § Arrival Sound Cue
If multiple whistles are on a Train, a player can only blow the Whistle at the frontmost of the Train. NPC Conductors can play every Whistle, however.

A
Stock Link
exposes a storage system to a
Logistics Network
, transmitting an inventory list to each of the other devices on the same network. The stock link also receives requests to extract inventory and passes the list on to an attached
Packager
to execute.
Contents

Recipe
Stock Link
Transmitter
+
Item Vault
Usage
[
]
Placement
[
]
A stock link must be attached to a packager to operate. It may be attached to either a side or top of a packager. The packager must be already attached to a storage block such as an
Item Vault
or chest.
Linking
[
]
Multiple stock links,
Stock Tickers
,
Redstone Requesters
, and
Factory Gauges
can be linked together into one or more
Logistics Network
. Placing a stock link will start a new network. To instead join the stock link to an existing network, hold the stock link and right click on any item already a part of the network. The stock link will glow purple. Upon placing it, Minecraft will display a message indicating the stock link is "tuned to this network."
Stock Links have no range limits and can work between dimensions, but the chunk they are in must be loaded in order for them to be seen by the network.
Operation
[
]
There are no manual interfaces to stock links. Once a stock link is placed, it operates completely automatically. All item requests must be created and sent by logistics network devices such as a stock keeper attached to a stock ticker.
A redstone signal fed to a packager will disable an attached stock link causing it to illuminate a red light.

Usage
[
]
Click a
Stock Link
with the Stock Ticker to connect it to that network. Place a
Mob
in a
Seat
or a
Blaze Burner
behind the Stock Ticker to turn it into a Stock Keeper.
Stock Keeper
[
]
The Stock Keeper can see all the items on the network. The UI displays how many
Stock Links
are connected. If the Stock Keeper is left unlocked, players can search the network, request items, and give their requests an
Address
to be sent to.
If the Stock Keeper is locked, other players will not be able to access its UI. The Stock Keeper will still be able to accept Shopping Lists.
Stock Categories
[
]
Categories for items can be set in the Stock Ticker’s UI. A
List Filter
or
Attribute Filter
can be used to create named categories including the items in the filters. This organizes the items in the Stock Keeper’s UI into named categories.
Shopping
[
]
Table Cloths
can be used to sell items.
Right click the Stock Keeper with a
Table Cloth
. Click items in the Stock Keeper’s UI to be sold on the
Table Cloth
, then click “configure” to confirm. Once the
Table Cloth
is placed, a price for the items can be set with any item.
A player can right-click
Table Cloths
with an empty hand to create a Shopping List of items to buy. Other
Table Cloths
can be clicked to add more items to the list. The list’s total price will be displayed in the Shopping List’s tooltip. The Shopping List can be sneak-clicked to be discarded.
Click a Stock Keeper with a Shopping List to buy the items. The price will be extracted from the player’s inventory and stored in the Stock Ticker, and the items will be requested from the Logistics Network to the
Address
set in the Stock Keeper’s UI.

Contraptions
